statements.label: supported
statements.text: APOBEC3-driven mutations in urothelial cancer were clonal and early, whereas chemotherapy produced bursts of hundreds of late subclonal mutations.
statements.evidence: We show that APOBEC3-induced mutations are clonal and early, whereas chemotherapy induces mutational bursts of hundreds of late subclonal mutations.
statements.note: The abstract contrasts the two mutational processes directly, including the order of magnitude of the chemotherapy-induced burst.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Patients whose tumours carried CCND1 ecDNA had shorter overall survival than patients whose tumours lacked it.
statements.evidence: Experimental modelling of CCND1 ecDNA confirmed its role as a driver of treatment resistance.
statements.note: A functional role in treatment resistance is shown, but no survival comparison between patients with and without CCND1 ecDNA is reported.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Most CCND1 amplifications in urothelial cancer were found to originate inside circular ecDNA-forming structural variants.
statements.evidence: We discovered that most CCND1 amplifications in urothelial cancer arise within circular ecDNA-forming SVs.
statements.note: This is stated as a direct finding about where the majority of CCND1 amplifications arise.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Over time ecDNA-forming structural variants persisted rather than disappearing, took up further DNA segments and became more complex.
statements.evidence: ecDNA-forming SVs persisted and increased in complexity, incorporating additional DNA segments and contributing to the evolution of treatment resistance.
statements.note: Persistence, added segments and rising complexity are all reported for the ecDNA-forming structural variants.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Dating of copy number alterations placed the onset of genomic instability decades before the tumour was diagnosed.
statements.evidence: Timing analyses on copy number alterations suggest that genomic instability emerges decades before tumour diagnosis
statements.note: The timing analysis reported in the abstract puts the emergence of genomic instability decades ahead of diagnosis.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The study analysed whole-genome sequences of 1,364 clinically annotated breast cancers, with transcriptome data available for most of those cases.
statements.evidence: we analysed whole-genome sequences from 1,364 clinically annotated breast cancers, with transcriptome data available for most cases
statements.note: The cohort size and the availability of transcriptome data for most cases are stated explicitly.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Whole-genome sequencing predicted which patients would relapse more accurately than standard clinical pathology did.
statements.evidence: highlighting their potential utility as predictive biomarkers for clinical evaluation of treatments such as CDK4/6 and HER2 inhibitors, as well as adjuvant and neoadjuvant chemotherapy.
statements.note: Biomarker potential is raised in general terms, but no head-to-head comparison with standard clinical pathology is reported.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Mutational signatures, homologous recombination deficiency, tumour mutational burden and heterogeneity scores were associated with clinical outcomes.
statements.evidence: Pattern-driven genomic features, including mutational signatures 2 , homologous recombination deficiency 3 , tumour mutational burden and tumour heterogeneity scores 4 , were associated with clinical outcomes
statements.note: These pattern-driven features are listed as showing associations with clinical outcomes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Faster speciation at low latitudes made the planktonic foraminiferal diversity gradient steeper.
statements.evidence: we find that higher rates of low-latitude speciation steepened the diversity gradient
statements.note: Higher low-latitude speciation rates are reported as steepening the gradient.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Terrestrial plant and insect clades acquired their modern latitudinal diversity gradients at the same time, around 15 million years ago.
statements.evidence: The latitudinal diversity gradient (LDG) is a prevalent feature of modern ecosystems across diverse clades 1-4 .
statements.note: The abstract notes that LDGs occur in many clades but reports timing only for planktonic foraminifera.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Across a 40-million-year record, a modern-style latitudinal diversity gradient in planktonic foraminifera appeared only 15 million years ago.
statements.evidence: Here we quantify the emergence of the LDG in planktonic foraminifera at high spatiotemporal resolution over the past 40 million years, finding that a modern-style gradient arose only 15 million years ago.
statements.note: Both the length of the record and the 15-million-year date of emergence are given as findings.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Species loss from high latitudes also reinforced the gradient, but this contribution was generally smaller than that of speciation.
statements.evidence: Extirpation of species from high latitudes also strengthened the LDG, but this effect tended to be weaker than speciation.
statements.note: The abstract reports both effects and ranks extirpation as the weaker of the two.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: RARE-seq detected tumour-derived cfRNA roughly 50 times more sensitively than whole-transcriptome RNA-seq, reaching a detection limit of 0.05%.
statements.evidence: we find RARE-seq to be approximately 50-fold more sensitive for detecting tumour-derived cfRNA than whole-transcriptome RNA sequencing (RNA-seq), with a limit of detection of 0.05%
statements.note: The fold difference against RNA-seq and the limit of detection are both stated in the analytical validation.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Platelet contamination substantially confounds cfRNA analysis, and an approach was developed to overcome it.
statements.evidence: We demonstrate that platelet contamination can substantially confound cfRNA analyses and develop an approach to overcome it.
statements.note: The confounding effect of platelets and the countermeasure are both reported.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Annual RARE-seq screening of asymptomatic smokers reduces lung cancer mortality.
statements.evidence: These results highlight the potential value of ultrasensitive cfRNA analysis and provide proof of concept for diverse clinical applications.
statements.note: Clinical potential is claimed only in general terms; no screening programme or mortality outcome is reported.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Detection of lung cancer expression signatures rose with stage, from 30% in stage I to 83% sensitivity in stage IV at 95% specificity.
statements.evidence: Detection of non-small-cell lung cancer expression signatures in cfRNA increased with stage (6 out of 20 (30%) in stage I; 5 out of 8 (63%) in stage II; 10 out of 15 (67%) in stage III; 80 out of 96 (83% sensitivity) in stage IV at 95% specificity)
statements.note: The stage-by-stage detection rates and the specificity threshold are given in the abstract.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In the Cambridge cohorts ecDNA was present in 24% of early-stage and 43% of late-stage Barrett's-associated oesophageal adenocarcinomas.
statements.evidence: In the Cambridge cohorts, the frequency of ecDNA increased between Barrett's-oesophagus-associated early-stage (24%) and late-stage (43%) EAC
statements.note: Both frequencies and the direction of the increase are stated for the Cambridge cohorts.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In biopsies taken before cancer diagnosis, ecDNA levels were higher in patients who later developed oesophageal adenocarcinoma than in those who did not.
statements.evidence: In biopsies that were collected before cancer diagnosis, higher levels of ecDNA were present in samples from patients who later developed EAC than in samples from those who did not.
statements.note: This comparison between future cases and non-cases is reported directly.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Screening Barrett's oesophagus biopsies for ecDNA identifies patients needing earlier surgery better than current histological grading does.
statements.evidence: In the cohort from the Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center, 33% of patients who developed EAC had at least one oesophageal biopsy with ecDNA before or at the diagnosis of EAC.
statements.note: ecDNA is detected before diagnosis, but the abstract never compares it with histological grading as a surveillance test.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: ecDNAs carried varied sets of oncogenes and immunomodulatory genes and gained copy number and structural complexity in more advanced disease.
statements.evidence: We found that ecDNAs contained diverse collections of oncogenes and immunomodulatory genes. Furthermore, ecDNAs showed increases in copy number and structural complexity at more advanced stages of disease.
statements.note: Gene content and the stage-related rise in copy number and complexity are both reported findings.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: cf-EpiTracing detected colorectal cancer earlier than standard faecal immunochemical testing in the same patients.
statements.evidence: Together, these findings establish cf-EpiTracing as an automated, non-invasive, epigenome-centric framework with broad applications in early diagnosis, molecular subtyping and prognostic prediction.
statements.note: Early diagnosis is claimed as an application, but no comparison with faecal immunochemical testing or any other established test is reported.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The study produced 2,417 cf-EpiTracing profiles from the plasma of 125 healthy individuals and 549 patients with one of four diseases.
statements.evidence: We generated 2,417 cf-EpiTracing profiles from plasma of 125 healthy individuals and 549 patients with inflammatory bowel disease, colorectal cancer, coronary heart disease or lymphoma.
statements.note: The number of profiles and the composition of the cohort are stated explicitly.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Following epigenetic signatures over time revealed transformation of follicular lymphoma into diffuse large B cell lymphoma.
statements.evidence: Surveying dynamics of epigenetic signatures uncovered disease transformation from follicular lymphoma to diffuse large B cell lymphoma.
statements.note: The transformation was uncovered by tracking the dynamics of the epigenetic signatures.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The platform identified primary diseased tissues and other organ involvement, separated B cell lymphoma subtypes, and picked up early-stage diseases or lesions.
statements.evidence: cf-EpiTracing enabled unbiased identification of primary diseased tissues and other organ involvement, stratification of B cell lymphoma subtypes with different genetic and epigenetic underpinnings, and detection of early-stage diseases or lesions.
statements.note: All three capabilities are listed as results of the cf-EpiTracing analysis.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Parental H3K9me3 goes mainly onto the leading strands of replication forks, above all at LINE retrotransposons oriented head-on to fork movement.
statements.evidence: H3K9me3 is preferentially transferred onto the leading strands of replication forks, which occurs predominantly at long interspersed nuclear element (LINE) retrotransposons (also known as LINE-1s or L1s) that are theoretically transcribed in the head-on direction with replication fork movement.
statements.note: The strand preference and its concentration at head-on LINEs are the paper's central reported observation.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The HUSH complex binds the leading-strand polymerase Pol ε and contributes to the asymmetric segregation of H3K9me3.
statements.evidence: the human silencing hub (HUSH) complex interacts with the leading-strand DNA polymerase Pol ε and contributes to the asymmetric segregation of H3K9me3
statements.note: The interaction and its contribution to asymmetric segregation are reported as the mechanism.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Mice lacking the HUSH complex develop tumours as a result of LINE de-repression.
statements.evidence: Loss of silencing of the repeat elements leads to genome instability and human diseases, including cancer and ageing 1-3 .
statements.note: The link between repeat de-repression and cancer is cited as background; no animal model or tumour outcome is reported here.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Cells lacking the Pol ε subunits POLE3 and POLE4, or the HUSH components MPP8 and TASOR, showed weakened H3K9me3 asymmetry and raised LINE expression.
statements.evidence: Cells deficient in Pol ε subunits (POLE3 and POLE4) or the HUSH complex (MPP8 and TASOR) show compromised H3K9me3 asymmetry and increased LINE expression.
statements.note: Both consequences of the deficiencies are stated for the same cells.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Across 947 tumour regions and 96 tumour-adjacent normal samples, the transcriptome emerged as a major source of phenotypic variation.
statements.evidence: Analyses of 947 tumour regions, representing both primary and metastatic disease, alongside 96 tumour-adjacent normal tissue samples implicate the transcriptome as a major source of phenotypic variation.
statements.note: The sample counts and the conclusion about phenotypic variation are given together.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: RNA single-base substitution signatures traced to ADAR and APOBEC3A activity exposed ongoing APOBEC activity that had otherwise gone undetected in these tumours.
statements.evidence: We extract signatures of RNA single-base substitutions and link their aetiology to the activity of the RNA-editing enzymes ADAR and APOBEC3A, thereby revealing otherwise undetected ongoing APOBEC activity in tumours.
statements.note: The signature extraction, the enzymes assigned and the newly revealed APOBEC activity are all reported.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Tumours with greater transcriptomic heterogeneity responded worse to immune checkpoint inhibitors in this cohort.
statements.evidence: Intratumour heterogeneity (ITH) fuels lung cancer evolution, which leads to immune evasion and resistance to therapy 1 .
statements.note: Immune evasion and therapy resistance appear only as background motivation; no checkpoint inhibitor treatment response is analysed.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Copy number-independent allele-specific expression was frequent and linked to epigenomic dysfunction, and it produced parallel genomic and transcriptomic evolution converging on cancer gene disruption.
statements.evidence: We observe frequent copy number-independent allele-specific expression that is linked to epigenomic dysfunction. Allele-specific expression can also result in genomic-transcriptomic parallel evolution, which converges on cancer gene disruption.
statements.note: Both the frequency and epigenomic link and the parallel-evolution consequence are reported findings.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: An Alu element inserted in a TBXT intron pairs with a neighbouring reverse-orientation ancestral Alu and generates a hominoid-specific alternative splicing event.
statements.evidence: We demonstrate that this Alu element-inserted into an intron of the TBXT gene 7-9 -pairs with a neighbouring ancestral Alu element encoded in the reverse genomic orientation and leads to a hominoid-specific alternative splicing event.
statements.note: The pairing of the two Alu elements and the resulting hominoid-specific splicing are demonstrated in the study.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Loss of the tail improved walking efficiency in the tailless mouse models.
statements.evidence: with a proposed role in contributing to human bipedalism 4-6 .
statements.note: A role for tail loss in bipedalism is mentioned as a prior proposal; no locomotion measurements in the mice are reported.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Mice carrying the exon-skipped Tbxt isoform developed neural tube defects, a condition occurring in roughly 1 in 1,000 human newborns.
statements.evidence: mice expressing the exon-skipped Tbxt isoform develop neural tube defects, a condition that affects approximately 1 in 1,000 neonates in humans 10
statements.note: The phenotype in the mice and the human incidence figure are both stated.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Mice expressing both Tbxt isoforms had either no tail or a shortened tail, depending on the relative abundance of the isoforms in the embryonic tail bud.
statements.evidence: Mice expressing both Tbxt isoforms exhibit a complete absence of the tail or a shortened tail depending on the relative abundance of Tbxt isoforms expressed at the embryonic tail bud.
statements.note: The dose-dependent tail phenotype is reported for the mouse models.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In the 110 patients given risk-adaptive treatment, three-year failure-free survival was 89.1% after a median follow-up of 47.3 months.
statements.evidence: After a median follow-up of 47.3 months, the 3-year FFS was 89.1% (83.2-95.0%) in the RAT group (n = 110).
statements.note: The follow-up time, the group size and the three-year failure-free survival are all given.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Failure-free survival was significantly better with risk-adaptive treatment than in the external cohort that did not receive it, with a hazard ratio of 0.41.
statements.evidence: Patients who received RAT showed significantly improved FFS (P = 0.003, log-rank test) compared with the no-RAT external cohort (hazard ratio = 0.41 [0.23-0.75]; P = 0.004, Cox regression model).
statements.note: The comparison against the no-RAT cohort, its significance and the hazard ratio are reported.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The risk-adaptive strategy reduced treatment costs compared with standard-of-care chemoradiotherapy.
statements.evidence: Collectively, these data show that a ctDNA-driven RAT paradigm could be a promising strategy to improve survival, challenging the conventional fixed-course, static treatment approach.
statements.note: The abstract argues for a survival benefit over fixed-course treatment but never measures or compares costs.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Tolerance of the risk-adaptive strategy was good and no deaths were attributed to the treatment.
statements.evidence: The RAT strategy was well-tolerated with no treatment-related deaths.
statements.note: Both tolerability and the absence of treatment-related deaths are stated.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Population genetic analysis found signatures of positive selection on rs112233623-T in Sardinia, a region where malaria was formerly prevalent.
statements.evidence: Using population genetic methods, we observe signatures of positive selection for rs112233623-T in the genetic history of Sardinia, a region in which malaria was once prevalent.
statements.note: The selection signature and the Sardinian malaria history are both reported.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The rs112233623-T allele breaks a SMAD3 binding site, weakens enhancer activity, lowers CCND3 expression in erythroblasts and blocks the G1-S transition.
statements.evidence: We show that rs112233623-T disrupts a binding site for the transcription factor SMAD3, weakens enhancer activity and, in erythrocyte precursors (erythroblasts), is associated with reduced CCND3 expression and inhibition of the G1-S cell-cycle transition
statements.note: Each step of this chain is reported as a result in the abstract.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Carriers of rs112233623-T admitted to hospital with malaria had lower mortality than non-carriers.
statements.evidence: Our results suggest that a reduction in CCND3 in erythroblasts constitutes a mechanism of resistance to malaria, and could enable therapeutic interventions.
statements.note: Resistance is inferred from cultured erythrocytes and population genetics; no patient outcomes such as mortality are reported.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Plasmodium falciparum grew less well in cultured erythrocytes from rs112233623-T carriers, and the degree of impairment tracked ROS levels.
statements.evidence: we show that parasite growth is impaired in cultured Plasmodium falciparum-infected erythrocytes from rs112233623-T carriers, and that this impairment correlates with ROS levels
statements.note: Impaired parasite growth in carrier erythrocytes and its correlation with ROS are both reported.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Integrating over 10 million single-cell and spatial spot transcriptomes from carcinomas and melanomas yielded nine broadly conserved spatial ecotypes.
statements.evidence: By integrating over 10 million single-cell and spot-level spatial transcriptomes from diverse human carcinomas and melanomas, we identified nine SEs with broad conservation
statements.note: The data volume and the number of ecotypes identified are stated directly.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The cfDNA-based ecotype assay selected patients for immunotherapy better than PD-L1 immunohistochemistry.
statements.evidence: Our data reveal fundamental units of TME organization and demonstrate a multimodal platform for profiling solid and liquid TMEs, with implications for improved risk stratification and therapy personalization.
statements.note: Improved stratification is offered as an implication, but no comparison with PD-L1 immunohistochemistry or any other clinical assay is reported.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: DNA methylation profiling distinguished the spatial ecotypes, and deep learning recovered them from plasma cell-free DNA.
statements.evidence: Notably, SEs were distinguishable by DNA methylation profiling and were recoverable from plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA) using deep learning.
statements.note: Both the methylation-based distinction and the cfDNA recovery by deep learning are reported.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In cfDNA from nearly 100 melanoma patients, levels of the spatial ecotypes showed strong associations with immunotherapy response.
statements.evidence: In cfDNA from nearly 100 patients with melanoma, SE levels exhibited striking associations with immunotherapy response.
statements.note: The cohort size and the association with immunotherapy response are stated.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Grade 2 histology accounted for 73% of primary astrocytoma samples and 93% of primary oligodendroglioma samples.
statements.evidence: Most primary surgery samples were classified as grade 2 on the basis of histology (73% for astrocytomas and 93% for oligodendrogliomas).
statements.note: Both percentages are given for the primary surgery samples.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Recurrent oligodendrogliomas newly acquired PI3K and NOTCH1 mutations irrespective of treatment, and these came with an increased tumour mutational burden.
statements.evidence: Mutations in phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K) and NOTCH1 were newly acquired in recurrent oligodendrogliomas, regardless of treatment, and were associated with an increased tumour mutational burden.
statements.note: The newly acquired mutations and their association with higher mutational burden are reported for recurrent oligodendrogliomas.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Patients with oligodendroglioma survived longer after recurrence than patients with astrocytoma.
statements.evidence: In both types of IDH-mutant glioma, we observed a convergence of acquired alterations, genome-wide changes and worse patient outcomes, suggesting that treatment-refractory clones were being selected.
statements.note: Outcomes are tied to acquired alterations within each tumour type, but survival is never compared between the two types.

statements.text: Temozolomide treatment was linked to the SBS11 and SBS119 signatures in both tumour types, whereas the radiotherapy-associated ID8 signature rose only in astrocytomas.
statements.evidence: Treatment with temozolomide was associated with the mutational signatures SBS11 and SBS119 in both tumour types, whereas the radiotherapy-associated ID8 signature increased in astrocytomas specifically.
statements.note: The abstract assigns these signatures to the two treatments and notes that ID8 increased specifically in astrocytomas.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The loss of recombination in R. tenuis reduces its capacity to adapt to changing environments.
statements.evidence: Meiotic recombination ensures accurate chromosome segregation and promotes genetic diversity by generating crossovers between homologous chromosomes 1 .
statements.note: The role of recombination in generating diversity is background; no measurement of adaptive capacity in R. tenuis is reported.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Both male and female meiosis in R. tenuis are obligately achiasmate genome-wide, with synapsis failing and univalents persisting at metaphase I.
statements.evidence: we show that R. tenuis undergoes obligate, genome-wide achiasmy in both male and female meiosis. Despite normal early meiotic axis formation, synapsis fails, crossovers are undetectable cytologically and genetically, and univalents persist at metaphase I.
statements.note: Genome-wide achiasmy in both sexes and the cytological details are reported findings.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Transposable elements accumulating on one haplotype skew segregation in favour of the larger, repeat-rich chromosomes.
statements.evidence: Haplotype-specific accumulation of transposable elements generates segregation distortion favouring the transmission of larger, repeat-rich chromosomes.
statements.note: The haplotype-specific transposable element load is reported as the source of the transmission bias.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Viable seeds form only when translocation-compatible gametes meet, so all surviving offspring are genetically identical.
statements.evidence: fertilization yields viable seeds only when translocation-compatible gametes meet, indicating strong post-meiotic selection against incompatible homozygous combinations. As a result, all surviving offspring are genetically identical
statements.note: Post-meiotic selection on gamete compatibility and the genetic identity of surviving offspring are both reported.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Feeding assays reproduced D. sechellia's preference for noni, while calcium imaging showed sweet sensitivity conserved and bitter sensitivity altered.
statements.evidence: Using quantitative feeding assays, we recapitulate the preference for noni in Dsec and detect conserved sweet but altered bitter sensitivity by means of calcium imaging in peripheral taste neurons.

statements.text: Noni activates bitter-sensing neurons more strongly in D. sechellia than in the two generalist species, owing to a small deletion in one gustatory receptor.

statements.note: The stronger bitter-neuron response in the specialist and its receptor-level cause are stated directly.

statements.text: Differences in dietary preference were mirrored by species-specific handling of noni and sucrose signals in sensorimotor circuits rather than by peripheral physiology.
statements.evidence: we show that instead of peripheral physiology, species-specific processing of noni and sucrose signals in sensorimotor circuits recapitulates differences in dietary preference

statements.text: BPDCN skin tumours appeared first at sun-exposed body sites and carried clonally expanded mutations caused by ultraviolet radiation.

statements.text: In colibactin-positive cancers, ID18 accounted for about a quarter of APC driver indels, linking colibactin exposure to APC driver mutations.

statements.text: ctDNA was detected within 120 days of surgery in 25% of patients, covering 49% of all patients who went on to relapse clinically.

statements.text: Neoantigens arising after whole-genome doubling were more often lost from the progressing liver metastasis than those arising before it.
statements.evidence: Neoantigens arising post-WGD were more likely to be absent in the progressing liver metastasis than those occurring pre-WGD
statements.note: The abstract compares loss of post-WGD and pre-WGD neoantigens in the progressing metastasis.
